description_full: Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz, together with its subsidiaries, provides payments, marketplace, and fintech solutions for consumers and merchants in Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, and Ukraine. The company operates through three segments: Payments, Marketplace, and Fintech. The Payments segment offers a platform that facilities transactions between and among merchants and consumers. This segment provides ways for consumers to pay for shopping transactions and regular household bills, as well as make peer to peer payments; and enables merchants to accept payment online and in store, issue and settle invoices, pay suppliers, and monitor merchant turnover. It also offers proprietary data, which facilitates informed decision-making across multiple areas of business. Its Marketplace Platform segment connects both online and offline merchants with consumers, enabling merchants to increase sales through an omnichannel strategy and allowing consumers to purchase products and services from various merchants. This segment operates marketplaces through m-commerce, a mobile solution for shopping in person; e-Commerce, which allows consumers to shop anywhere and anytime with free delivery; and Kaspi Travel that allows consumers to book domestic and international flights, domestic rail tickets, and international package holidays. It also enhances merchants' sales by connecting payments and fintech products, Kapsi advertising, and other delivery services. The Fintech Platform segment provides consumers with buy-now-pay-later, finance and savings products, and merchants with merchant finance services. It also involved in the banking; distressed asset management; real estate business; payment processing; online travel; e-grocery; classifieds; and storage and processing of information services. Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in Almaty, the Republic of Kazakhstan.

financial_summary: Joint Stock Company Kaspi.kz -  is a large-cap technology business with a $17.1B market cap on $9.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +36% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -12.5pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 305% against a 10% cost of capital — a 295-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $1.1B in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.63×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
